#deck:The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book::Chapter 01 - Introduction
HPML Ch 1 — What is machine learning in this book's practical definition?
column2:
Gathering examples and algorithmically building a statistical model to solve a practical problem.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What information does a supervised-learning dataset contain?
column2:
Pairs (x_i, y_i): an input feature vector and its target label.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is a feature vector?
column2:
An ordered collection of values describing an example; each coordinate has a consistent meaning across examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the goal of supervised learning?
column2:
Learn a model that maps an input to a label, or to information from which a label can be deduced.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What distinguishes unsupervised learning from supervised learning?
column2:
Its training examples do not include target labels; the algorithm learns useful structure or representations.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does a clustering model assign to an example?
column2:
A cluster identifier indicating a group of related examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the output of dimensionality reduction?
column2:
A representation with fewer features than the original input vector.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does an outlier-detection score describe?
column2:
How atypical an example is relative to the data; the score's numerical direction depends on the implementation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What data does semi-supervised learning use?
column2:
Both labeled and unlabeled examples, often with many more unlabeled examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — Why can unlabeled data help semi-supervised learning?
column2:
It reveals the input distribution or structure, which may improve learning from limited labels; this is not guaranteed.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does a reinforcement-learning policy map?
column2:
A representation of the environment's state to an action, aiming to optimize a long-term reward objective.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.4.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What distinguishes reinforcement learning from one-shot supervised prediction?
column2:
Actions can affect later states and rewards, so decisions are sequential and consequences extend into the future.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.4.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does one feature record in the chapter's binary bag-of-words example?
column2:
Whether a particular dictionary word occurs: 1 if present, 0 otherwise; repeated occurrences do not increase the value.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — In bag-of-words encoding, what determines input dimensionality?
column2:
The dictionary size, not the number of documents.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is a decision boundary?
column2:
The boundary between regions of input space assigned different predicted classes.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the chapter's linear SVM prediction rule?
column2:
Predict sign(w* dot x - b*), where the starred parameters were learned during training. A zero score needs a tie convention.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the canonical hard-margin SVM constraint?
column2:
For every example with y_i in {-1, +1}: y_i (w dot x_i - b) >= 1.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — How does canonical SVM margin width depend on ||w||?
column2:
The full width is 2/||w||. Subject to the canonical constraints, a smaller norm gives a larger margin.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — Besides accuracy, which two runtime costs matter when choosing an algorithm?
column2:
The time to build/train the model and the time to process predictions.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What sampling assumption supports the chapter's generalization intuition?
column2:
Training and future examples should come from the same data-generating process, with independent and representative sampling. Distribution shift can break this intuition.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.4.
